bullets.title: META: Strong Q3/Q4 beat but stock -3% premarket on capex scale and equity raise overhang
bullets.body: META Q3 revenue $64.6B (+26% YoY) beat by ~2% with EPS $7.40 vs $6.54 consensus; Q4 guided $73-76B (2pt FXN acceleration). FY26 capex raised to $135-145B and a new Class C non-voting share structure (2:1 split effective Jan 2027) signals an equity raise as early as Jan 2027 at 'hundreds of billions' scale for AI/Muse. Muse has 10M+ US/Canada deployments with 25% daily engagement; analysts cluster PTs $800-885 (90% Buy) but stock reversed from +5% post-earnings to -2-3% on the capital raise and geopolitical risk-off.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q3 beat on margins but capex cut to $20B and SpaceX merger chatter weigh; stock -4-5%
bullets.body: TSLA Q3 EPS $0.48 beat $0.42-0.45 estimates; total gross margin 19.6% vs 18.5% forecast; auto GM ex-credits 18.1% vs 16.3%. Revenue $28.0B missed GS estimate by 4%. Capex guidance cut to ~$20B from $25B, disappointing given robotics/AI ambitions. Cybercab deployed in Austin with 2M cumulative unsupervised miles (8x QoQ); FSD attach >75% NA deliveries, 1.74M active subs. Piper raises PT to $475, Mizuho to $460, JPM to $430; GS lowers '26/'27 EPS to $0.67/$1.60.

bullets.title: SPOT: Q3 beats on subs/margins, Q4 guide better than feared; stock +5-6%
bullets.body: Spotify Q3 premium subs 306M (+6M net adds, 1M above guide); gross margin 33.0% (+136bps YoY, beat guide 32.9%); operating income €672M beat. Q4 gross margin guided 33.8% (better than feared), operating income €820M well above MS €773M and JPMe €770M; premium subs guidance 316M. Ad revenue €482M slightly missed. MS, JPM, UBS, Wolfe, Citi, Keybank all maintain Buy/OW with PTs $620-$680. 2027 increasingly flagged as monetization inflection year.

bullets.title: TXN: Blowout Q3 beat-and-raise; Industrial/Data Center/Auto all accelerating; stock dips AH
bullets.body: TXN Sep-Q revenue $6.06B (+2% beat), EPS $2.62 vs $2.41-2.42 consensus; gross margin 64.2% vs Street 61.6-61.8%. Dec-Q guided $5.80-6.30B midpoint +5% above consensus extending above-seasonal streak to 10 quarters. Industrial +40% YoY hit all-time peak; Data Center nearly doubled YoY; Autos accelerated to mid-teens. CY27 analog pricing negotiations underway; Citi raises CY26/27/28 EPS, maintains Buy $345 PT. Stock dipped AH despite clean print, with CY27 thesis seen as intact.

bullets.title: LRCX: Dec-Q guide disappoints vs elevated bar; supply constraints cost $300M+; stock -7-8%
bullets.body: LRCX F1Q beat modestly but F2Q revenue guide came in below buyside expectations; gas delivery subsystem shortages and cleanroom bottlenecks could cost $300M+ in the Dec quarter. Company raised CY26 WFE outlook to mid-$150B and provided preliminary CY27 WFE of >$200B (+28%) with 10 new Tier-1 fabs online. China revenue expected meaningfully lower in Dec Q. Citi cuts PT to $435 but lifts FY27/28/29 EPS; views selloff as buying opportunity at ~15-16x C2028E.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Q3 beats on EBITDA/FCF/EPS but broadband subs and wireless miss; stock +1.7-2.5%
bullets.body: CMCSA Q3 revenue $29.30B beat, adj. EBITDA $9.11B beat $8.87B consensus, EPS $1.07 beat $0.99, FCF $4.21B crushed $3.3B consensus. Domestic HSD net adds -143K slightly worse than -130K estimate; wireless adds 368K missed 399K. Peacock swung to +$261M EBITDA from -$217M a year ago; paid subs ~48M. UBS maintains Neutral at 5x fwd EBITDA; KeyBanc Underweight PT $18 (~4.6x '27 EBITDA). Bears flag broadband ARPU decline -2.9% YoY and Orlando Parks weakness.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO confirms supply/deployment speed as binding constraint; Vera Rubin cycle building
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO stated manufacturing and deployment speed remain the binding constraint on AI; new supply agreements target multi-year capacity increases through 2028. Vera Rubin cycle picking up; TSMC 3nm remains the biggest bottleneck. LG Innotek announced a robotics sensing collaboration with NVDA for physical AI solutions to debut at CES/GTC. Separately, TSLA and NVDA to jointly invest KRW3.7T ($2.8B) in Samsung Electro-Mechanics.

bullets.title: NBIS: Secures $3.5B Citi financing facility for data center/GPU build-out
bullets.body: Nebius secured a $3.5B, 364-day facility from Citi at SOFR+275bps (max 3.50%) for data center development, GPU procurement, and general corporate purposes. Management cited $40B+ in long-term customer contracts as collateral base for additional asset-backed financing. Stock -3.3% premarket amid broader AI infrastructure selloff; Piper has mixed views on FY27 guidance.

bullets.title: TEAM: Multiple analysts raise PT to $275 on cloud/AI acceleration; Q1FY27 expected +3-5% beat
bullets.body: Atlassian PT raised to $275 by both Oppenheimer and OPCO (from $200) on cloud growth accelerating to ~34%, strong JSM/Rovo AI adoption, and Rovo transitioning to metered pricing in December. Checks show steady seat expansion and rising cross-sell in Teamwork Collection; MCP Server and Teamwork Graph supporting AI narrative. Bear case on AI disruption removed.

bullets.title: MU: HBM4 in high-volume manufacturing; NAND G11 ramp targets 2H27
bullets.body: Micron confirmed HBM4 is in high-volume manufacturing with HBM4E samples already shipping. NAND strategy skipping G10 to jump directly to G11, targeting 2H27 ramp with 2x bit density, 1.5x faster I/O, and >400 layers. DA Davidson reiterates Buy citing technology leadership and wide moat. JPM views MU as a Buy on AI memory growth thesis.

bullets.title: GLW: Enterprise segment >75% YoY growth; Morgan Stanley EW on capex-constrained margins
bullets.body: Corning's Enterprise segment is expected to grow more than 75% YoY in Q3 (vs. 65% in Q2), driven by hyperscaler relationships including Meta and NVIDIA-backed builders. However, elevated capex (~$2B FY26, up from $1.7B) and ramp costs are expected to limit margin expansion. Apple confirming all iPhone/Apple Watch cover glass made in Kentucky by YE26. Long-haul/DCI represents a ~$1B annual opportunity potentially materializing well ahead of 2030. MS maintains Equal-Weight.

bullets.title: T: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW, cuts PT to $25 from $28 on higher rates/Starlink risk
bullets.body: AT&T Q3 service revenue +3.8% YoY, adj. EBITDA +5.4%; added 442K fiber subs (beat 390K) and raised FY26 EPS guidance +4% to $2.40 midpoint. Fiber ARPU down 4% YoY from introductory pricing headwinds. PT cut from $28 to $25 on higher interest rates and Starlink competitive risk, but MS views the ~6-7% stock selloff as an overreaction. Mexico exit expected to close Q1 2027.

bullets.title: GOOGL: RDDT data deal renewal uncertain; Search trends slowing; virtual power plant expansion
bullets.body: JPM notes GOOGL-RDDT $60M annual data deal faces renewal uncertainty with investor probability 'down very low.' Channel checks indicate GOOGL Search trends slowed at quarter-end, implying ~1-point revenue growth miss. Separately, Google and Voltus expanded their virtual power plant agreement to 1GW in PJM (up from 100MW in June), and Google Cloud now offers OpenAI models, the only hyperscaler with access to top-3 closed-source LLMs.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wolfe downgrades to Peer Perform from Outperform
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's Peter Supino downgraded Netflix to Peer Perform from Outperform with the stock at $65.04. JPM notes bears expect FY27 revenue guide below Street and potential deal-making needed to sustain growth.

bullets.title: CLS: Investor Day expected to guide FY27 ~$38.9B revenue (+80% YoY) with potential capital raise in 2H27
bullets.body: Celestica is expected to guide FY27 revenue ~$38.9B at its upcoming Investor Day, well above Street consensus of $35.7B, with ~9% operating margins. JPM models ~$3B FCF outflow in 2027 on heavy capex and working capital; a potential capital raise decision could come in 2H27. META's capex guidance raise to $135-145B is a direct read-through for Celestica's AI infrastructure business.

bullets.title: DDOG: Consensus expects ~34-35% Q3 revenue growth; AI/hyperscaler seen as exponential tailwind
bullets.body: Datadog is expected to report Q3 revenue growth of 33-35% YoY, with Q4 high-end at +30-31%. The broader business ex-largest customer grew ~36% YoY in Q2; enterprise new-logo bookings doubled YoY. MS notes Q3 bar is ~33-34% despite largest customer headwind. JPM and Jefferies both flag DDOG as a well-liked software stock with AI as an exponential tailwind; investors need core non-OpenAI revenue to accelerate.

bullets.title: WDC: UBS expects significant outperformance in Sep and Dec quarters on HDD demand
bullets.body: UBS models Western Digital Sep-Q revenue $4.27B and EPS $4.40 vs Street $4.56B/$4.76 — citing HDD demand strength. Dec-Q forecast $5.03B revenue and EPS $5.93 vs Street. Incremental gross margins seen in the 80s. WDC and OMC expected to report after the close.

bullets.title: DKNG: Prediction market share reaches 4.6%, surpassing Crypto.com for first time
bullets.body: DraftKings' prediction market share reached 4.6%, surpassing Crypto.com (4.5%) for the first time, though Kalshi still leads at 63.4%. NFL hold tracking in line with expectations; Supreme Court decision on the prediction market case could come December-February with oral arguments March-April. UBS notes SRAD NBA prediction market deal is now fully in guidance.

bullets.title: NET: cRPO accelerates to 35% YoY; DBNRR improves 2pp to 120%; surpassed 10M developers
bullets.body: Cloudflare's cRPO growth accelerated to 35% YoY; Dollar-Based Net Retention improved 2pp QoQ to 120%; developer platform surpassed 10M users vs 7.4M in Q2. Strength broad-based in CDN/Application Security and Workers/Developer Platform. MS maintains OW; Jefferies flags PANW/NET/CRWD as having the most appealing 2027 cybersecurity setups.

bullets.title: Broad AI/semi sector risk-off: SOXX -3.6%, neo-clouds -3-5%, quantum -4%; geopolitical catalyst
bullets.body: Pre-market selling accelerated across AI infrastructure (CRWV -3.5%, NBIS -3.3%, IREN -4.2%), quantum (IONQ -4.2%, QBTS -3.6%, RGTI -4.1%), and nuclear (SMR -4.4%, OKLO -3.8%). Catalysts include Iran kinetic-risk chatter post-election, META/TSLA capex uncertainty, and AI return-on-investment skepticism. Hedgeye warns AI bubble is deflating; NYSE/NASDAQ have had net new lows outnumber highs for 37-38 consecutive days, a historically bearish signal.
